structured.approach: I followed the data-engineering-steps skill for DE-05. First I fetched both contracted inputs, task.components (e777bda) and org.data_model (a6b3e2a), through context_get to get receipts. Then I fetched the DES-02 output feat.design through context_get as background, because DE-04 points to its DC-1, DC-2 and B1.2 to B1.4 sections for the record and delay shapes. I compared the registered Invoice entity field by field against the source contract (feed v2 → v3) and against the current transform.to_model code in the tool view. The step changes the data model only, so I made no code change. The code for the change belongs to the TC-1 and TC-2 budgets in the later coding step, so I did not run ahead of the task plan. I ran the CI once on the unchanged branch to record a green baseline. I wrote feat.data_model_change.md and had the verifier subagent check it. I fixed the three findings it raised: approval wording now cites the journey board, step IDs that no cited source names are gone, and the workbook action and gate text now cite record:brief.

claims.text: The registered Invoice entity already holds paid_date as date or None, noted as added in feed v3, beside id, vendor, due_date, amount (Decimal, 2 dp) and paid.
transform.to_model does not produce paid_date yet; its docstring lists only id, vendor, due_date, amount and paid, so paid_date is registered but not yet implemented.
Feed v3 adds the optional paid_date column, and ingestion needs no code change because csv.DictReader keys each row by its header; a v2 feed keeps loading.
The Rejected row gains the new reason value 'paid_date', which reaches reject_reasons through dq.quality_report with no change to dq.
The new derived Delay history is Dict[str, List[int]]. It holds only paid records that have a paid_date, with delay_days = (paid_date - due_date).days, in feed order, and negative values are kept.
paid_date is validated only after the existing field checks pass, and an unpaid record with a valid paid_date keeps it. The design still marks both rules as pending.
No storage, database or schema migration is involved; the Delay history stays in memory.
Amounts stay Decimal and are never converted to float.
The ap_pipeline package version today is 0.4.0.
CI on the unchanged feature/story branch passed: 3 tests run, 0 failures, coverage 100.0.

open_questions: Should the registered org.data_model be extended with the Rejected row reason value 'paid_date' and the Delay history structure? Today it describes only the Invoice entity. (Owner: data engineering lead / data modelers; non-blocking)
Carried from DE-04 (CQ-I1): is the feed v3 column spelled exactly 'paid_date'? (Owner: feed owner; non-blocking; this output assumes 'paid_date')
Carried OQ-B6 / DD-7: should an unpaid record keep a valid paid_date? (Interim answer: it is kept and the Delay history ignores it; non-blocking)
Carried DQ-4: should delays_by_vendor be re-exported from ap_pipeline/__init__.py? (Interim answer: no; non-blocking)
structured.summary: The DE-05 data model change for FEAT-ZD-48600 is written to outputs/FEAT-ZD-48600/feat.data_model_change.md. The registered Invoice entity already includes paid_date (date or None, feed v3), and I confirmed it field by field against the feed contract and the current code. paid_date is registered but transform.to_model does not produce it yet; the TC-1 change implements it. I added two items the registered model does not hold yet: the Rejected-row reason value 'paid_date' and the derived in-memory Delay history Dict[str, List[int]], which delays_by_vendor produces and ap_forecast consumes. The output also covers knowledge-graph relations, compatibility (feed v2 still loads and no key or signature changes) and schema validation rules for the unit-test step. Nothing is removed or retyped, and there is no storage or migration. I changed no code in this step. CI on the unchanged branch passes. There are no blocking questions; the main open question is whether to register the two new structures in org.data_model org-wide.
